cim: Shontel Brown introduces legislation to regulate AI-generated campaign content
cim_eredeti: Shontel Brown introduces legislation to regulate AI-generated campaign content
szoveg_eredeti:
COLUMBUS, Ohio — Congressperson Shontel Brown, D-OH, introduced legislation to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in election campaign content.

The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act aims to prohibit the use of AI to deprive or defraud individuals of their right to vote. It also seeks to require disclaimers on AI-generated content.

In the midst of the midterm election season, candidates have increasingly used artificial intelligence for advertisements, with over $130 million in AI-generated ads streaming this election year. According to Wesleyan University, 69% of ads with AI content do not have disclaimers.

“This isn’t complicated: voters deserve to know that the campaign content they see and hear is real. We need labels on AI-generated election content and we need to hold accountable those who use AI to knowingly spread false information," Brown said in a news release. "Pairing the latest technology with old-school dirty tricks is a dangerous combination. I’m proud to introduce the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act and will continue to defend the voting rights of every American."

Brown’s office points to concerns of deepfake advertisements and the spread of false information through artificial intelligence, including the deliberate spread of incorrect voting procedures. She first introduced this legislation in 2024.

The legislation would be enforced by the Federal Trade Commission and applies to federal, state and local campaign content. For more information and to track the progression of the bill, click here.
